newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police threaten to close rebel party HQ.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police threaten to close rebel party HQ.

text.p: Police have threatened to close the week-old headquarters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, the Jakarta Post said on Wednesday.
National Police Chief Dibyo Widodo was quoted as saying it was only a matter of time before the authorities moved to close down the office.
Officials at the new headquarters had not had any contact with police and the office remained open on Wednesday morning.

Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding President Sukarno, opened the office last week after her supporters were evicted from the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a police raid on July 27.
Supporters loyal to Megawati had refused to give up the headquarters after a government-sponsored PDI congress in June deposed Megawati and elected deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi in her place.
The raid sparked the worst riots in Jakarta for over two decades in which at least five people died and scores of buildings and vehicles were set ablaze.
Megawati said the congress was unlawful and illegal as she had been elected PDI leader for a five year term in 1993.
Earlier this week, the government refused to accept a list of nominations submitted by Megawati for next year's parliamentary elections, saying it only recognised the PDI faction headed by her rival.
She is currently a member of parliament, but will be unable to run in the 1997 elections.
